findings.summary: the per-cascade caster matrices were selected by a ternary written out in both PALs -- Dawn spelled the test twice inline, SDL named it `cascaded` -- so the fallback rule lived in two places and had already started to drift; one `shadow_caster_matrices` in `pal_gpu_shared.hpp` answers for both, and it keys on the generator's own FILTER rather than on whether a layer index happens to be in range, refusing an unfitted cascade by name instead of silently rendering through a pair a cascaded generator never writes

`ShadowGeneratorRecord::task` became duplicate state the moment a generator grew `caster_tasks`: one writer (`= caster_tasks.front()`), two readers, and both readers immediately hopped through the task to reach its TARGET. It is a `map_target` handle now, which is what the receiver's texture lookup actually wants, and "has this generator been built" has one spelling instead of two

Dawn grew a `shadow_uniform_sizes` vector beside `shadow_uniforms` that stored exactly `shadow_refresh.blocks[handle].size` -- a parallel array to resize, write and keep in step with the block it mirrors, and one that silently assumed a generator's block size never changes. The bind reads the block the refresh already holds

`record.depth_layers == 0 ? 1u : ...` was restated in both PALs, where `create_render_target` already normalises it and the record's member initialiser is 1 -- two copies of a rule that reads as "zero is possible here" and sends the next reader looking for the case that produces it

the layer mechanism was general in texture creation but shadow-only in attachment: `task.render.depth_layer` was honoured inside the shadow branch alone, so an ordinary pass into a layered target would have written layer 0 while the record said otherwise. Both PALs' depth-only passes take the layer now, and Dawn's vacuous `depth_layer_views[i] : depth_view` fallback is gone -- `depth_view` IS layer 0

`ShadowCascade::near_plane`/`far_plane` were write-only: the pin reads its `_near`/`_far` only for `csmWorldBiasClipOffset`, which is the `worldSpaceBias` arm this port refuses, so they were dead by construction rather than by oversight. Two fields and their two stores are gone

the cascade count was clamped in the fit but not in `build_shadow_task`, which read the raw record field -- so `numCascades: 8` would have built eight layers and eight caster passes against four fitted cascades. The emitted factory clamps where the pin clamps (`Math.min(cfg.numCascades ?? 4, 4)`), after which the fit, the layered map and its passes all read one already-clamped count

`csm_max_cascades` and `csm_default_num_cascades` were emitted as two literals plus a contract error asserting they agree -- belt, braces and a comment explaining they are different concepts. The assertion is gone: the clamp fixes the receiver block's `array<mat4x4, MAX>` and the `??` fixes what a scene naming no count gets, and neither is derived from the other

`cfgDefault` was `optionDefault`'s body with the initializer swapped, which is the third copy of the two tests `LoweringContext.nullishDefault` exists to hold. One `nullishDefaultValue` takes the initializer and each caller says where it found it -- a `const` local, or a property of the pinned config literal

`assertCsmUboLayout`'s tail carried a special case for float 77 in both the condition and the error message, because the ternary it reads is a magnitude rather than a shape. Seeding the expected map with that index and deleting it in the branch makes the tail the same four lines `assertShadowUboLayout` ends with, one function over

the change deleted the file's ONLY tie to the pinned declaration -- `context.functionDeclaration(csmHooksModule, "_computeCsmCascades")`, whose comment read "Anchor the adapted fit to the exact camera-frustum function it mirrors" -- leaving ~250 lines of mirrored C++ with nothing checking the split, the slice, the ortho or the texel snap against upstream. `assertCsmCascadeFit` matches eleven of the pin's own expressions plus the caster-Z tighten and the CSM hook's `_bias * 0.5` clip offset (which is what licenses reusing the PCF family's already-lowered `bias_view_projection`), so a formula that moves upstream refuses generation by name

`ensureCsmShadowTaskState` had no contract assertion where both its siblings do, while `build_shadow_task` claimed to mirror its per-layer construction. That construction is now held to the pin's own `clr: true`, `dFormat: "depth32float"`, `_depthCompare: "less-equal"`, `_ownsDepthTexture: false`, its single-layer `createView({dimension: "2d", baseArrayLayer: i, arrayLayerCount: 1})`, and the `i <= (mesh._shadowMaxCascade ?? i)` cap whose identity arm is what makes ignoring `setShadowCasterMaxCascade` consistent

the SDL bone-palette sweep walks every draw list, and a cascaded generator contributes one list per cascade holding the same casters -- so a skinned caster streamed its palette once per cascade per frame, each an extra transfer buffer, copy pass and full command-buffer submit. The sweep dedupes by mesh, which also retires the pre-existing main-list/shadow-list duplicate

`shadow_receiver_bytes` memcpy'd into a fixed-width array with nothing bounding the source, so a future third block shape would have overflowed silently instead of failing generation; the bound is a `static_assert` now. That also settles where the size belongs: the SDL vertex stage pushes the block's BYTES, so a `{bytes, size}` carrier exists whatever the reflected row says, and putting a size on the row as well would be a second source with nothing checking the two agree

the cascade fit should be LOWERED from `_computeCsmCascades`'s own AST rather than mirrored, the way `compute_directional_light_matrix`, `build_light_view_matrix`, `multiply_4x4` and `bias_view_projection` in the same file are -- CSM is otherwise the only shadow family whose per-frame math is re-typed

Lowering it needs new lowerer capability rather than a rearrangement of this change, and that capability has no measurement behind it yet. The mirror is guarded in the meantime by the thirteen pinned expression shapes recorded three findings above

the packaged asset kept 20.7 MB of Gaussian-splat ellipsoid attributes that nothing referenced any more, against 11.0 MB of converted rows — the conversion CONSUMES primitives where the sibling passes rewrite accessors, so an asset whose only primitives were GS ones reaches its binary chunk through nothing at all. `readsBinaryChunk` asks the four members that can name a bufferView for presence (unknown readers answer yes), and where it answers no the rows become the whole chunk and the accessors that described the consumed attributes go with the bytes. Scene 226's packaged GLB fell from 31.8 MB to 11.0 MB, which is also 3x less startup I/O

`BinaryBuilder.append` copied every appended buffer twice — a view, then a copy of the view — which is an 11 MB memcpy for a splat row buffer; the builder holds a view now, with the invariant its callers already satisfy stated on it

the emitted loader validated its own generation's output (`rotation.size() != 3u` throwing on a value this compiler wrote), while skipping the BIN bounds check its sibling bufferView reader performs — the one check that shipped was the one that could not fire.
